stem: Which of the following is an example of an action tool, as opposed to an information-retrieval tool?

options.text: A tool that retrieves the current date
A tool that looks up a word's dictionary definition
A tool that places a real purchase order
A tool that searches a knowledge base for relevant text passages

explanation.why_correct: Placing a real purchase order causes a persistent, real-world side effect (money charged, an order created), which is the defining characteristic of an action tool.

why_incorrect.B: Looking up a dictionary definition only retrieves and returns information, with no real-world side effect -- a read-only information tool.
why_incorrect.D: Searching a knowledge base for text passages returns information without causing any external side effect, making it a read-only tool.
why_incorrect.A: Retrieving the current date is a pure information lookup with no side effect on any external system.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Action tools cause real, persistent side effects (orders, payments, deletions); information tools only retrieve and return data with no side effect.

stem: A model was trained with data up to a certain date. A user asks about an event that occurred one week after that date. What is the correct conclusion?

options.text: The event cannot possibly be real since the model wasn't trained on it
The model will automatically know about the event because one week is a short time
The model cannot know about this event from training alone and would need a tool to retrieve current information to answer accurately
The model should simply guess with full confidence since the gap is small

explanation.why_correct: Regardless of how short the gap is, any event occurring strictly after the training cutoff is, by definition, unknown to the model from training alone -- a tool-based lookup is needed to answer accurately.

why_incorrect.B: The length of the gap doesn't matter for this logical point -- even a very short gap still means the event occurred after the training cutoff and is therefore unknown to the model.
why_incorrect.D: Guessing with full confidence about something the model has no actual knowledge of is a recipe for false confidence and risks presenting an unfounded answer as fact.
why_incorrect.A: The event's real-world existence is entirely independent of whether the model was trained on information about it; many real events are simply unknown to a model with an earlier cutoff.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Any event after a model's training cutoff is unknown to it from training alone, regardless of how small the time gap is -- a tool lookup is needed for accurate current information.

stem: A high-stakes financial report requires several facts, some stable (basic accounting definitions) and some current (today's specific exchange rate). What is the most appropriate approach?

options.text: Use a tool call for every single fact in the report, including the stable definitions
Use internal knowledge for the stable definitions and a grounded tool lookup for the current exchange rate
Use internal knowledge for everything, including the current exchange rate
Refuse to produce the report because it contains a mix of fact types

explanation.why_correct: This matches the appropriate principle of selective tool use: stable, well-established facts can safely come from internal knowledge, while the current, rapidly changing exchange rate specifically benefits from a grounded tool lookup.

why_incorrect.C: Relying on internal knowledge for the current exchange rate risks a stale, possibly significantly wrong value in a high-stakes financial context.
why_incorrect.D: A mix of fact types doesn't require refusal; it simply requires applying the right approach (tool vs. internal knowledge) to each type of fact.
why_incorrect.A: Using a tool for every fact, including stable definitions that don't need it, adds unnecessary overhead without a corresponding benefit.

explanation.rule_of_thumb: Match the approach to each fact's actual nature -- internal knowledge for stable facts, grounded tool lookups for current or high-stakes changing facts.
